recipes.name: Lentils And Spinach
ingredients_raw: 2 white onions, halved and sliced into 1/2 rings
freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Saute onion for 10 minutes or so, until it begins to turn golden. Add minced garlic and saute for another minute or so.

Add lentils and water to the saucepan. Bring mixture to a boil. Cover, lower heat, and simmer about 35 minutes, until lentils are soft ( this may take less time, depending on your water and the lentils).

Meanwhile cook the spinach in microwave according to package directions. Add spinach, salt and cumin to the saucepan. Cover and simmer until all is heated, about ten minutes. Grind in plenty of pepper and press in extra garlic to taste.

raw_recipe.headline: Lentils And Spinach
raw_recipe.description: This is my own adaptation of an Indian recipe. It doesn't look like much, but it is surprisingly yummy. Serve this for dinner over hot rice or a diced baked potato. Pair with carrots, cauliflower, or a fresh sliced tomato for a full meal.

review.reviewBody: This was seriously good. I used 1 cup of red lentils, and 2.5 cups of vegetable broth in place of the water specified. I also used half a white onion, half a red onion, four cloves of garlic, and during the last five minutes, wilted fresh spinach directly on top of the lentils, along with the remaining salt, pepper, cumin and garlic specified in the recipe. Got rave reviews from vegetarians and meat-eaters alike. Excellent recipe!

It came out really well, and my family of meat eaters were pleasantly surprised. I used 1 cup of lentils which is the right amount, vegetable broth in place of water, chopped up a few baby carrots and threw them in, also thew the spinach in during the last 10 mins of the lentils simmering (because 1 pot is better than 2 or unnecessarily using a microwave). I put the dish over a Black and Brown rice I prepared. Dish was easy and delicious, clean up was easy.

I used chicken stock instead of water and curry powder instead of cumin. I also used fresh baby spinach (just added it to the lentils at the end of cooking time) instead of frozen spinach. I made this last night and am eating leftovers for lunch today, and it's even better today!

This recipe is a keeper! My son recently became vegan, and he loves it. Myself, as a meat eater, I think this is a great recipe!

However, I amped up the ingredients. The lentils come in one pound bags, which = 5 cups. So, I use the whole bag, and use 10 cups of vegetable broth (actually 8 cups, or two boxes of veggie broth, and 2 cups water. What am I gonna do with leftover two cups of veggie broth, right?) Then, I add several chopped carrots, and some chopped celery right at the end of the sauteing the onions/garlic. I also use 10 oz fresh spinach rather than frozen, and just toss it in.

Also, like another reviewer suggests, I used two onions: one sweet and one red.

Wonderful! It's a meal in itself. This is really really good. And be careful, my modifications make a LOT of lentils, so be sure to use an 8 quart pot or bigger. The leftovers get devoured, so you can get many meals out of this.

This was outstanding! It’s definitely worthy of the rave reviews. I made some substitutions based only on what I had on hand. I used diced red onion that was leftover from yesterday’s brunch, as well as diced yellow pepper because I didn’t want it to go to waste. I used homemade chicken broth instead of water as well since I always make lentils or rice with broth instead of water. Finally, I used fresh spinach because I had some leftover from the farmers market. I just added it in the last five minutes and wilted it down. Everything else I kept as is. The final result smelled amazing cooking and it tasted great. Cheap, tasty and healthy! I do recommend doubling the recipe if you plan to eat this as a main dish. I halved the recipe intending to have a little leftover for lunch, but I definitely could eat it all in one sitting.

This was fantastic. I made it for my vegan niece that was staying with us (swapped the veg oil for olive). Used 2 large yellow onions, doubled the lentils, cumin, and garlic. Added a tsp of turmeric, used fresh spinach, and veg broth instead of water. Added a can of diced tomatoes half way through cooking time. It was so good I made it for hubby and I and added sausage. Flavors are out of this world.

Very delicious and very easy. I made it with some of the reccomendations of the other reviewers: Doubled the lentils to 1 cup and increased the seasonings: 2 tsp of cumin , 1 tsp of celery seed and 1/8 tsp of cayenne (I also soaked my lentils for a half hour before I cooked them up) . This dish will become a standard in my kitchen - Thanks!

I made this as-is the first time and really liked it, but felt it was better the second time when I wilted fresh spinach into it in the last 5 or so minutes of cooking the lentils instead of using frozen spinach. I felt like the frozen made it a little mushier than it should be.

I've been making this for years. Some changes I sometimes make. Add bell pepper, celery and/or carrots at the beginning. My kids don't like chunks so sometimes I hit it with a hand blender before I add the lentils. I've added stewed tomatoes. I always add lemon juice at the end. Always use chicken broth. I love it poured over a slice of Swiss cheese.

LOVE this! Here are the adjustments I make after having made it a few times:
- double the lentils
- use 2-2.5 cups vegetable or chicken broth instead of water
- use fresh spinach (put in at end) instead of frozen and let wilt
-add a can of diced tomatoes about halfway through cooking of the lentils
- if I have it, I add cilantro when I add spinach

WOW! I was looking for a lentil recipe besides the typical soup. This was great b/c I had all the ingredients on hand. It turned out so good. I used coconut oil for the onions, used broth and water, upped the cumin, added tumeric (beautfil color), used fresh spinach, and added some carrots, too. This was the main feature in our meatless meal. Served with toasted pita bread and olive oil. My husband and 3 boys all loved it. They said it was exotic, but delicious. It was SO easy!
Update: I make this regulary, and when I do not have fresh spinach, I use canned. You must put the canned spinach in for a longer time to get the canned taste out; it's the only way we eat canned spinach, actually.
I substituted fresh spinach and used only one onion because that was all I had on hand. Still good!
This was great! I followed the advice of others and used 1 cup of lentils and 2.5 cups of vegetable broth, and I omitted the salt (the broth had plenty).

I used at least a quart of vegetable stock to make this dish more flavorful, and added more as needed to make the consistency of a soup. This has been a great option for both vegetarian and vegan guests.

This is soooo good! I love it and tend to eat it with rice pilaf. I've added come curry along with the cumin. Also used broth instead of water. It is tasty! It's filling and most excellent to eat on a cold day!
When I was caregiver for my elderly mother she wanted to go out to eat every day. When I did cook she would not eat it ….except when I made this! I believe she ate two bowls full
I found it tasteless and watery. I did use green lentils which might have made some difference. I even added some garam masala which helped, but....no!

We are trying to eat healthier meals, and this was a good one! I used 1/2 cup lentils, but next time I'll use a full cup. I added 1 chopped carrot, 1/2 diced red pepper, 1/2 diced green pepper, 1 can diced tomatoes, and some Penzeys Singapore Seasoning (in addition to the ground cumin). I also added fresh baby spinach at the end rather than frozen. Delish!
This is one of our fav dishes we use vegetable broth instead of water and add a tablespoon of tomato paste. We also finish with fresh grated parmesan and some franks hot sauce !
